user.title: Connect to TypeSafe
user.description: Paste an API key from your TypeSafe account. Home Assistant asks one short question to check that the key works.

data_description.api_key: The key the requests are sent with. Leave it empty only for an endpoint of your own that needs no key.

data_description.url: Leave this alone unless you run something of your own that speaks the same API, such as a proxy that holds the key or caches answers. The key is sent as a bearer header, so an http address puts it on the wire in clear.
data_description.model: The model id sent with every request. Clear it to use the default.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-enter your API key
reauth_confirm.description: TypeSafe rejected the key currently stored. Paste a working one. The API address is left as it is; use Reconfigure to change that.

data_description.api_key: Requests go to the API address already stored.

reconfigure.title: Replace your API key or address
reconfigure.description: Paste a different TypeSafe API key, and change the address if the API is reached somewhere other than TypeSafe. Your questions and entities are kept.

data_description.api_key: Leave it empty to keep the current key while the address stays the same. A new address gets no key unless you type one.

data_description.url: Clear this field to go back to the TypeSafe API. The key is sent as a bearer header, so an http address puts it on the wire in clear.
data_description.model: The model id sent with every request. Clear it to use the default.

error.cannot_connect: Home Assistant could not reach the API at that address.
error.not_found: The server answered HTTP 404. Jev adds /v1/systemone to the address, so give only the part before that. For OpenRouter that is {openrouter_url}.
error.invalid_url: That is not a usable API address. It needs a scheme and a host, and it cannot carry a space, a query, a fragment, a username or a password.
error.invalid_model: That model id was not accepted. Check it, or clear the field to use the default.
error.key_required: The TypeSafe API needs a key. An empty key only works with an address of your own that needs none.

abort.already_configured: This API key is already set up. An entry is identified by its key, so a second address needs its own key.

init.title: Spending limits
init.description:
Input tokens are what you pay for, and question text counts as input. Set the budget past anything a working setup would use, so only a runaway reaches it. Zero means no limit.

The conversation agent sends anything it is unsure about to the fallback agent, whole and with nothing done first. Leave it empty and it will say it did not understand. Whole-house commands are refused unless you allow them, except for turning everything off, which is always allowed.

data.daily_token_budget: Daily input token budget (0 = no limit)
data.price_per_million: Price per million input tokens, in USD
data.min_confidence: Act only above this confidence (0 to 1)
data.allow_whole_home: Allow commands that name no room or device

data_description.daily_token_budget: Counted from midnight in the Home Assistant time zone. 0 means no limit.
data_description.price_per_million: Sets the estimated cost sensor and the cost in the question preview. Nothing that is sent depends on it.
data_description.fallback_agent: Receives the whole sentence when Jev is not sure what to do.
data_description.min_confidence: Below this, Jev does nothing and passes the command to the fallback agent.
data_description.allow_whole_home: Turning everything off is always allowed, with or without this.

daily_budget_exceeded.title: Jev stopped evaluating: daily budget reached
daily_budget_exceeded.description: The daily budget is {budget} input tokens and {used} have been used today. The next evaluation, of context {context}, needs about {estimate} more and does not fit, so no further questions are being asked. The answer sensors go unavailable until a call fits again. Raise the budget in the integration options, evaluate contexts less often, or shorten your questions.

daily_budget_spent.title: Jev stopped evaluating: daily budget reached
daily_budget_spent.description: The daily budget is {budget} input tokens and {used} have been used today, so no further questions are being asked. The answer sensors go unavailable until the day rolls over or the budget is raised. Raise the budget in the integration options, evaluate contexts less often, or shorten your questions.

noul.name: Ask a yes/no question
noul.description: Ask whether something is true and get the probability of yes, from 0 to 1. Use one of these per label when several labels can be true at once.

state.name: State
state.description: The text to judge. Write a template and it is rendered before it is sent.

instructions.name: Question
instructions.description: Phrase it so that a high number means yes. A statement works as well as a question.

true_means.name: Yes means
true_means.description: Optional. What counts as a yes. Worth filling in when the boundary is subtle.

false_means.name: No means
false_means.description: Optional. What counts as a no.

threshold.name: Threshold
threshold.description: Where to draw the line for the is_true field in the response. The probability itself is always returned as well. A value near 0.5 means the model cannot tell, not that the answer is half true.

config_entry.name: API key
config_entry.description: Which configured key to ask with. Only needed when more than one is set up.

include_attributes.name: Include all attributes
include_attributes.description: Off by default. Sends every attribute of the picked entities, not just the value, unit, device class and area. A weather forecast or a media player artwork list runs to thousands of tokens, and you pay for them on every evaluation.

background.name: Background
background.description: Optional. Standing facts about how to read this, such as what a reading means for your particular device. It travels with the question rather than the readings, which measurably works better than putting it in the state. An object rather than a sentence keeps your own key names, and the model reads those keys.

choice.name: Pick one option
choice.description: Pick one option from your list, and get the probability of every option plus a confidence value.

state.name: State
state.description: The text to judge. Write a template and it is rendered before it is sent.

instructions.name: Question
instructions.description: What the model is choosing between, in one sentence.

options.name: Options
options.description: Two to 255 options. Include a catch-all such as other when your list might not cover every input.

option_descriptions.name: Option descriptions
option_descriptions.description: Optional. A description per option, which sharpens the boundary between similar ones. Saying what an option excludes helps most.

score.name: Rate on a scale
score.description: Rate the text against levels you describe, and get a number that can land between two levels.

instructions.name: Question
instructions.description: One dimension per question. A question measuring three things at once produces a low confidence and a meaningless middle.

levels.name: Levels
levels.description: Two to 10 levels, lowest first. Describe a concrete situation for each, not a degree: Broken but there is a workaround beats Moderately severe. Each level is judged on its own, so comparative wording and numbers in the text do nothing.

ask.name: Ask several questions at once
ask.description: Ask any mix of question types about one piece of text, in a single request. Every question is judged independently against the same text and they run in parallel, so twenty questions take about as long as one.

state.name: State
state.description: The text to judge. Write a template and it is rendered before it is sent.

questions.name: Questions
questions.description: Your own key for each question, then its type of noul, choice or score, its instructions, and criteria for choice and score. The keys are yours: they come back as the keys of the answers and the model never sees them.

config_entry.name: API key
config_entry.description: Which configured key to ask with. Only needed when more than one is set up.

nothing_to_judge.message: Nothing to judge: give this action some text, or pick the entities, devices or areas it should look at.

no_entry.message: No loaded Jev config entry to ask with. Add the integration first, or pick one under API key when more than one is set up.

entry_ambiguous.message: More than one Jev entry is loaded: {entries}. Pick one under API key, because each entry has its own key and budget.

missing_targets.message: These targets do not exist: {targets}. Asking about the rest would answer a different question from the one you wrote.

empty_target.message: That target holds no entities, so there would be nothing to judge.

too_many_entities.message: That target holds {count} entities and the limit is {limit}. Every entity is billed as input on every evaluation, so pick the ones the question turns on, or split it.

question_shape.message: Question {key} needs both 'type' and 'instructions'. Types are noul, choice and score.

wrong_answer_type.message: Asked a {question_type} question and got a {got} back, which the API should not do.

choice_options_out_of_range.message: A choice takes {min} to {max} options and this one has {count}.

score_levels_out_of_range.message: A score takes {min} to {max} levels, lowest first, and this one has {count}.

unreadable_answer.message: TypeSafe returned an answer of type {kind}, which this version cannot read. Update the integration.

task_needs_structure.message: Task {task} asks for free text, and Jev answers typed questions only. Give the action a structure whose fields are booleans, selects or numbers.

task_over_budget.message: Task {task} costs about {estimate} input tokens and {remaining} of the {budget} daily budget are left. Raise or clear the budget in the integration options to continue.

reserved_field.message: The field {field} cannot be used, because the result carries the confidence behind every answer under that name. Rename the field.

answer_missing.message: The reply carries no answer for {field}.

unsupported_field.message: Field {field} uses a {selector}, and Jev answers a yes/no question, a pick from a list, or a rating on a scale. Give the field a boolean, a select with its options, or a number with a min and a max.

field_options_out_of_range.message: Field {field} offers {count} options, and a pick needs {min} to {max}.

field_needs_scale.message: Field {field} is a number with no {bound}. A rating needs both ends of the scale.

field_scale_not_ordered.message: Field {field} has min {min} and max {max}, which is not a scale.

answer_does_not_fit.message: The answer to {field} came back as a {answer}, which does not fit a {selector}.

context_template_failed.message: The state template for context {context} failed: {reason}

context_over_budget.message: Evaluating context {context} costs about {estimate} input tokens and {remaining} of the {budget} daily budget are left. Raise or clear the budget in the integration options to continue.

common.not_understood: Sorry, I did not understand that.
common.whole_house: That would affect the whole house. Say which room or which device you mean.
common.which_kind: Which kind of thing do you mean? Say the lights, or the switches, or name a room.
common.preview_grouped: Sent in one request together with: {others}.
common.preview_cost: Asked once for this preview: {tokens} input tokens, about ${cost}, {ms} ms.
common.preview_threshold_over: That is above your threshold of {threshold}, so the binary sensor would be **on** right now.
common.preview_threshold_under: That is below your threshold of {threshold}, so the binary sensor would be **off** right now.
common.preview_undrawable: The answer came back in a shape this version cannot draw.
common.preview_unbuildable: That question cannot be built yet: {reason}
common.preview_rejected: TypeSafe rejected the API key, so there is no trial answer.
common.preview_mismatched: The API answered, but not to the question that was asked.
common.budget_spent: The daily token budget is spent, so I cannot do that today.
common.auth_failed: TypeSafe rejected the API key. Check it in the Jev settings.
common.unavailable: TypeSafe did not answer. Try again in a moment.
common.preview_over_budget: The daily token budget is spent, so there is no trial answer. The question still saves.
common.preview_nothing_yet: No trial answer: there is nothing to ask about yet.
